- If sentiment is consistently low or neutral (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or shift downward by 1–3%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), model tends to ignore it — adjust forecast to align with recent 7–14 day moving average.
- If sentiment history shows rising bullish sentiment (e.g., >0.3 over 3+ days), model often underestimates upside — increase forecast by 1–2% per sentiment unit above 0.2.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overfits recent trend — apply smoothing or decay factor (e.g., 0.85) to recent 7-day average to reduce overconfidence.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after high sentiment, model often fails to anticipate — add 1–2 day lag correction (forecast 1–2 days below true drop) if sentiment drops sharply.
